terminal.description: A shell in your workspace: node run.mjs <file> runs the query in that file against a fresh copy of the practice's database and prints the rows.

tasks.title: Show every animal
tasks.description:
Winnie wants to see every animal the practice knows.

In `queries/1-every-animal.sql`, write one query that returns every row and every column of the `animals` table.

Check runs your query against the data you can see and against a hidden set of animals, and compares the columns and the rows that come back.
nextSteps: Run `node run.mjs queries/1-every-animal.sql` once and read what it prints today.
Find the `animals` table in `schema.sql` and look at its columns.
Write your query below the comments in the file.
Run the file again and look for Biscuit in the rows.
hints: The lesson's part "Asking with SELECT" shows a query that returns a whole table.
A query names what to give back, then which table to read. One symbol stands for every column.
The query has the shape `SELECT * FROM table_name;` with the name of the animals table in place of `table_name`.

tasks.title: Show every owner
tasks.description:
Next Winnie wants the people behind the animals.

In `queries/2-every-owner.sql`, write one query that returns every row and every column of the `owners` table.

Check runs your query against the data you can see and against a hidden set of owners, and compares the columns and the rows.
nextSteps: Write your query below the comments, the same way as in task 1.
Look at the `email` column: some owners show `NULL`.
hints: This is the same kind of query as task 1, about another table.
Only the table name changes. Copy it from `schema.sql` so every letter matches.
If SQLite says `no such table`, compare the name it shows with the name after `CREATE TABLE` in `schema.sql`.

tasks.title: Fix Ifan's query
tasks.description:
Ifan left a query that is meant to list every visit, but SQLite refuses to run it.

In `queries/3-fix-the-query.sql`, fix the query so it returns every row and every column of the `visits` table. Read each error SQLite prints and fix the spot it points at. Keep it one query.

Check runs your query against the data you can see and against a hidden set of visits, and compares the columns and the rows.
nextSteps: Run `node run.mjs queries/3-fix-the-query.sql` and read the error.
Fix only the spot the error points at, then run the file again.
Repeat until rows come back instead of an error.
Compare the table name with `schema.sql` letter for letter.
hints: SQLite stops at the first mistake it finds, so you fix them one at a time.
A `syntax error` near a word usually means that word, or the one just before it, is misspelt. Compare each keyword with the query in task 1.
There are three mistakes: two misspelt keywords and a table name that is not quite the one in `schema.sql`.
